Cryptococcal latex antigen was positive in serum and CSF, CSF fungal culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans, and skin punch biopsy with ABPAS stain confirmed cryptococcal yeasts -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Hematoxylin-eosin (Fig. 1B) and mucicarmine (Fig. 1C) stains of an endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspirate from the lymph node revealed many encapsulated yeast forms with narrow-based budding, morphologically consistent with Cryptococcus species, and no malignant cells.

rationale: A 57-year-old male with lymphoma on R-CHOP presenting with fever and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. EBUS-FNA of mediastinal lymph node stained with mucicarmine demonstrated encapsulated yeast forms with narrow-based budding consistent with Cryptococcus. Serum CrAg was 1:128, CSF CrAg was 1:128, and CSF culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: An air dried touch preparation was done of the leptomeningeal covering of the brain prior to fixation. This showed numerous cryptococci (Figure 2).

rationale: A 36-year-old woman with HIV-1 presenting with chronic headache and meningismus who died shortly after admission. Autopsy touch preparation of leptomeninges demonstrated numerous cryptococci, and histopathology of brain, lymph nodes, and ovary confirmed disseminated cryptococcosis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histological examination revealed collections of cryptococcal organisms lying within the superficial lamina propria, with an associated inflammatory infiltrate comprising abundant plasma cells, lymphocytes, and some histiocytes (see Figure 2).

rationale: A 66-year-old female on high-dose inhaled fluticasone presenting with hoarseness and vocal fold erythema. Microlaryngoscopy biopsy revealed collections of cryptococcal organisms in the lamina propria on histopathology, confirming laryngeal cryptococcosis. Successfully cured with oral fluconazole -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Aggregates of Cryptococcus organisms, as confirmed by periodic acid-Schiff and methanamine silver staining, lay in the surface inflammatory crust and within the subepithelial stroma (see Figures 4 and 5).
evidence_items.test_name: Vocal cord biopsy histopathology (PAS and GMS stains)

rationale: A 69-year-old female on inhaled fluticasone presenting with persistent hoarseness. Vocal cord biopsy histopathology demonstrated aggregates of Cryptococcus organisms confirmed by PAS and methenamine silver staining, and serum CrAg was positive at titer of 2. Successfully cured with fluconazole -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Latex agglutinin test revealed cryptococcal antigen in both cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum.
evidence_items.test_name: Latex agglutination test for cryptococcal antigen

rationale: A 21-year-old male lung transplant recipient on immunosuppression presenting with pulmonary infiltrates and yeast-like structures on lung biopsy. Latex agglutination test confirmed cryptococcal capsular antigen (CrAg) in both CSF and serum, satisfying E2 criteria. Successfully treated with liposomal amphotericin B and fluconazole -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cryptococci were detected in the CSF by the India ink staining, and CSF cryptococcal antigen titers were elevated.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF India ink staining and CrAg titer

rationale: A 75-year-old male with chronic myeloid leukemia on chemotherapy presenting with syncope and headache. India ink staining of CSF directly demonstrated cryptococci (E1 confirmatory), and CSF cryptococcal antigen titers were elevated (E2). Successfully treated with amphotericin B and flucytosine -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: From the sputum and blood culture we found Gram-positive cocci of Staphylococcus hominis and yeast cell of Cryptococcus neoformans (Figure 2).

rationale: A 43-year-old male with AIDS presenting with cough, shortness of breath, and somnolence. Blood culture confirmed yeast cells of Cryptococcus neoformans, fulfilling E1 confirmatory criteria. He was treated with fluconazole and antiretroviral therapy with clinical improvement -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The serum for cryptococcal antigen test was also positive. The diagnosis of biliary cryptococcosis was confirmed.

rationale: A 61-year-old female presenting with obstructive jaundice and hilar bile duct stricture. Successfully treated with fluconazole -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF cryptococcal antigen was positive, and later cultures also grew Cryptococcus neoformans.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF cryptococcal antigen and fungal culture

rationale: A 73-year-old female post-hip surgery and COVID-19 infection presenting with acute hydrocephalus. CSF cryptococcal antigen was positive (E2) and CSF cultures definitively grew Cryptococcus neoformans (E1 confirmatory). Successfully treated with amphotericin B and flucytosine along with CSF diversion -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cerebrospinal fluid India ink stain was completed in the early evening of hospital day 5 and showed rare encapsulated yeast, and the cerebrospinal fluid cryptococcal antigen (Latex Agglutination, IMMY, Inc., Norman, Okla., USA) was positive at a dilution of 1:32.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cryptococcal antigen was positive with a titer of 1:2048 and encapsulated budding yeast was seen from India ink examination (Fig. 2). CSF fungal culture revealed Cryptococcus gattii.

rationale: A 38-year-old male presenting with headache, progressive bilateral vision loss, papular skin lesions, and a cystic thalamic cryptococcoma. evidence_items.source_quote: Cryptococcus neoformans was histologically found as spherical or yeast-like organisms within the cytoplasm of macrophages, and no granulomas were seen (Figure 4).

rationale: A 69-year-old female kidney transplant recipient on long-term prednisone presenting with a painful calcaneal osteolytic mass and fever. Successfully treated with liposomal amphotericin B followed by fluconazole, satisfying E1 confirmatory histopathologic criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: On day 5, the 1st-day blood culture was reported to be positive for C. neoformans.

rationale: A 37-year-old female with SLE and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis admitted for uremic symptoms whose blood culture yielded Cryptococcus neoformans on day 5. Echocardiography revealed large (16x4 mm) mitral valve vegetations with severe regurgitation, confirming cryptococcal infective endocarditis and fungemia. Successfully underwent urgent bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement and IV amphotericin B plus flucytosine, satisfying E1 confirmatory blood culture criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: On the third hospital day, cryptococcal antigen from the LP returned positive as did the India ink stain.

rationale: A 70-year-old female presenting with subacute severe cognitive decline and chronic CD4 lymphopenia secondary to undiagnosed SLE. Successfully treated with IV amphotericin and high-dose fluconazole with complete recovery to baseline, satisfying E1 India ink and E2 CrAg criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cerebrospinal fluid examination revealed cryptococcal meningitis.

rationale: A 49-year-old male with advanced HIV infection (CD4 45 cells/microL) and pulmonary tuberculosis presenting with fever, severe headache, and dizziness. Diagnostic cerebrospinal fluid examination established the diagnosis of cryptococcal meningitis. The patient was treated with induction liposomal amphotericin B and fluconazole alongside anti-TB therapy, satisfying E1 confirmatory criteria for active cryptococcal meningitis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: serum and CSF point-of-care lateral flow assays were both positive for cryptococcal antigen (CrAg: Immuno-Mycologics [IMMY], Oklahoma, USA). evidence_items.test_name: Serum/CSF CrAg LFA and CSF India ink preparation

rationale: A 25-year-old female with advanced HIV infection presenting in coma with signs of meningeal irritation following non-adherence to antifungal maintenance therapy for prior cryptococcal meningitis. Diagnostic LP demonstrated positive point-of-care lateral flow assays for cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) in both serum and CSF, and India ink microscopy revealed numerous encapsulated budding yeast cells characteristic of Cryptococcus species. Confirmed recurrent cryptococcal meningitis (E1 microscopy, E2 antigen) treated with high-dose fluconazole -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: On day 3, serum Cryptococcal antigen of 1:64 was reported. Treatment for cryptococcosis was initiated with liposomal amphotericin B 350 mg intravenously daily and flucytosine 2,500 mg orally every 6 hours.

rationale: A 63-year-old male on long-term high-dose corticosteroid therapy presenting with severe headaches, gait collapse, and multiple ring-enhancing cerebellar lesions mimicking toxoplasmosis. Testing revealed a strongly positive serum cryptococcal antigen titer of 1:64 and positive CSF cryptococcal antigen titer of 1:4 with marked lymphocytic pleocytosis. Liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine therapy led to complete resolution of symptoms and radiographic edema, satisfying E2 strong antigen criteria -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 46-year-old female on long-term fingolimod for multiple sclerosis presenting with a painful chest wall mass, 7th rib osteomyelitis, and pathologic fracture. Core biopsy GMS stain revealed yeast forms, fungal cultures isolated Cryptococcus neoformans (serogroup A), and serum cryptococcal antigen was positive at a titer of 1:80. Successfully treated with liposomal amphotericin B, flucytosine, and fluconazole, meeting E1 confirmatory culture and E2 antigen criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histopathology revealed numerous spherical organisms that have a thick clear capsule and are surrounded by histiocytes forming a granuloma, multinucleated giant cells with spherical structures that have a clear mucoide capsule surrounding a central pale nucleus compatible with Cryptococcus [Figure 3].

evidence_items.specimen: craniocervical arachnoid and dura biopsy tissue

rationale: A 39-year-old male presenting with progressive quadriparesis, multiple lower cranial nerve palsies, and diffuse leptomeningeal thickening and cystic compression of the medullary bulb. Suboccipital craniectomy and biopsy histopathology demonstrated numerous encapsulated spherical yeast-like organisms with clear mucoid capsules in granulomatous tissue and multinucleated giant cells compatible with Cryptococcus, establishing E1 confirmatory histopathologic criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The mNGS of the liver specimen was conducted and the result revealed the identification of the sequence of C. neoformans, but the reads number was 1 and the reads per million ratios were 3.11%, which was the only etiological evidence.

rationale: A 48-year-old immunocompetent female presenting with elevated CA19-9 and multiple liver nodules mimicking metastatic carcinoma. Liver biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) definitively identified the genome sequence of Cryptococcus neoformans from the liver nodule specimen. Targeted antifungal therapy with oral fluconazole resulted in near-complete radiological resolution of hepatic nodules and biochemical remission, confirming E1 molecular diagnosis of hepatic cryptococcosis -> POSITIVE.

step4_condition_matched: Cryptococcal panniculitis / Cryptococcus neoformans var. grubii

The culture of biopsy from the leg's necrotic ulcer grew C. neoformans var. grubii.

rationale: A 36-year-old female renal transplant recipient on immunosuppression presenting with subcutaneous nodules and necrotic ulcers on her right lower extremity diagnosed with cryptococcal panniculitis. Direct India ink examination and fungal culture of aspirate were positive for cryptococcus, mucicarmine and PAS stains of skin biopsy demonstrated encapsulated yeasts with clear halos, and ulcer biopsy culture confirmed Cryptococcus neoformans var. grubii. Satisfies E1 confirmatory diagnostic criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A cryptococcal antigen titer was strongly positive (> 1:1 024).
Several days later, Cryptococcal species were identified as C. gattii.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF fungal culture and species identification

rationale: A 60-year-old immunocompetent male presenting with subacute headaches, weakness, fatigue, hyponatremia, and bilateral hearing loss. Lumbar puncture revealed opening pressure of 27 cm H2O, lymphocytic pleocytosis, and a strongly positive CSF cryptococcal antigen titer (>1:1024). Fungal isolation definitively identified Cryptococcus gattii. Successfully treated with amphotericin B and flucytosine. Meets E1 confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.test_name: Surgical pathology review and Cryptococcus antigen testing

rationale: A 30-year-old male presenting with new-onset focal seizures found to have intracranial mass lesions. Second opinion confirmed granulomatous inflammation with organisms consistent with Cryptococcus, and follow-up Cryptococcus antigen was positive. Meets E1 confirmatory criteria (mucicarmine-positive encapsulated yeasts) and E2 strong criteria (positive cryptococcal antigen) -> POSITIVE.

step4_condition_matched: Cryptococcal meningitis / Cryptococcus neoformans var. grubii

evidence_items.source_quote: Direct microscopic examination of CSF with India ink showed the presence of a large number of spherical yeasts surrounded by a clear haloed zone consistent with Cryptococcus spp. (Figure 1).

A lateral-flow immunochromatographic assay for the rapid and semiquantitative detection of Cryptococcus antigen (CrAg  LFA Immuno-Mycologics, Inc., OK, USA) revealed a low titre (1 : 40) in the CSF and a higher titre (1 : 160) in the serum.

Subsequently, the CSF, inoculated onto Sabouraud-chloramphenicol media without cycloheximide, incubated at 30 C, yielded smooth yeast colonies later confirmed as Cryptococcus neoformans var. grubii by matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization time-of-flight (MALDI-ToF) mass spectrometry using Bruker BioTyper instrument.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF fungal culture and MALDI-ToF identification

rationale: A 55-year-old male farmer presenting with headache, confusion, fever, and neck rigidity. Lumbar puncture revealed opening pressure of 35 cm H2O. CSF India ink examination showed encapsulated yeasts with clear halos, CrAg lateral flow assay was positive in CSF (1:40) and serum (1:160), and CSF culture confirmed Cryptococcus neoformans var. grubii by MALDI-ToF. Meets E1 confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cultures of the aspirate of the erythematous bullous lesion in the leg, and blood and CSF samples, obtained at the time of admission, yielded Cryptococcus neoformans.

evidence_items.source_quote: Analysis of the CSF with India ink was positive for Cryptococcus species.

evidence_items.source_quote: Period Acid-Schiff and mucicarmine stain revealed purple organisms and numerous budding yeasts consistent with Cryptococcus spp.

rationale: A 56-year-old male with multiple sclerosis on fingolimod presenting with cryptococcal meningitis. CSF was positive for cryptococcal antigen (1:1024), and fungal culture definitively identified Cryptococcus neoformans -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood cultures collected were also positive for Cryptococcus neoformans.

rationale: A 37-year-old female with HIV presenting with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and disseminated cryptococcosis. Blood cultures were positive for Cryptococcus neoformans, and CSF cryptococcal antigen was positive (>1:1024) -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 44-year-old male presenting with pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) secondary to anti-GM-CSF autoantibodies who developed disseminated cryptococcosis with elevated serum and CSF cryptococcal antigen titres -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 37-year-old liver transplant recipient with donor-derived Cryptococcus gattii complex infection. Nigrosin direct microscopy of CSF revealed encapsulated budding yeast and CrAg lateral flow assay was positive -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Additional serum cryptococcal antigen testing produced positive outcomes.

rationale: A 61-year-old male presenting with hip pain and iliac osteolytic lesion. Iliac bone biopsy high-throughput mNGS identified Cryptococcus neoformans (135,273 sequence reads; 99.73% relative abundance) and serum cryptococcal antigen was positive -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology findings confirmed the diagnosis of cutaneous cryptococcosis.
Cryptococcal serum antigen was elevated at 160 (ref <2).

rationale: A 69-year-old immunosuppressed female kidney transplant recipient on belatacept and mycophenolate presenting with an ulcerated cheek papule. Biopsy revealed a dense granulomatous infiltrate with innumerable encapsulated yeast forms, confirming cutaneous cryptococcosis on histopathology (E1). In addition, cryptococcal serum antigen was elevated at 160 (E2). Successfully treated with oral fluconazole -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood cultures returned positive for C. neoformans (Fig. 1).
Her blood and cerebral spinal fluid (CSF) cultures remained positive for C. neoformans (Fig. 1, Table 1).

rationale: A 21-year-old pregnant woman at 16 weeks of gestation with uncontrolled congenital HIV (CD4 9 cells/mm3) presenting with headache, photophobia, and disseminated cryptococcosis with cryptococcal meningitis. Blood and CSF cultures repeatedly grew Cryptococcus neoformans, satisfying E1 confirmatory criteria. Successfully managed with L-AmB and Amb-LC desensitization regimens -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: In August 2022, a 54-year-old man living with HIV, who was off ART at presentation, was diagnosed with CM caused by Cryptococcus neoformans var neoformans in our department.
Identification of C. neoformans var. neoformans was performed by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization-time of flight (MALDI-TOF).

rationale: A 54-year-old male living with HIV diagnosed with cryptococcal meningitis caused by Cryptococcus neoformans var neoformans. Organism confirmed via MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry (E1) along with high CSF and serum CrAg titers (1:1000). Successfully maintained on isavuconazole as secondary prophylaxis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cryptococcus neoformans  was rapidly identified on CSF analysis on hospital Day 1 (Day 1), leading to a diagnosis of DC.
Postmortem examination revealed cryptococcal infiltration within the myocardial interstitium and capillaries, accompanied by microemboli (Figure 3A).

rationale: A 34-year-old male with untreated HIV presenting with septic shock and severe myocardial dysfunction requiring VA-ECMO. Cryptococcus neoformans was identified on CSF analysis, and autopsy confirmed disseminated cryptococcal infiltration within myocardial tissue and microemboli, fulfilling E1 confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The serum cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) titer was positive at 1:20.

rationale: A 56-year-old male former miner with Caplan syndrome presenting with recurrent fever, chest pain, and pulmonary nodules. Serum cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) was positive at 1:20 titer (E2 strong evidence), responded to fluconazole therapy, and subsequently rebounded to 1:10 upon corticosteroid tapering, demonstrating active cryptococcal antigenemia -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: MALDI-TOF MS (Bruker) confirmed C. neoformans (score: 1.9) (Figure 4B).

rationale: A 23-year-old immunocompetent male presenting with severe community-acquired pneumonia due to MRSA and Cryptococcus neoformans coinfection. India ink examination of BALF sediment showed classic round encapsulated budding yeasts with refractile halos, and MALDI-TOF MS definitively confirmed C. neoformans (E1 confirmatory criteria). Successfully treated with fluconazole and linezolid -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 25-year-old male with untreated HIV/AIDS presenting with headaches, weakness, oral thrush, and GI symptoms. CSF analysis was positive for cryptococcal antigen (titer 1:512), and fungal culture confirmed Cryptococcus neoformans. Duodenal biopsy also revealed cryptococcal organisms consistent with chronic duodenitis. Successfully treated with induction amphotericin and flucytosine followed by fluconazole, satisfying E1 confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Both CSF culture and mNGS (the relative abundance of Cryptococcus neoformans was 20.45%) confirmed Cryptococcus neoformans infection, with no other pathogens detected.

rationale: A 69-year-old male with membranous nephropathy on immunosuppressive therapy presenting with two months of intermittent fever and headache. Serum Cryptococcus neoformans capsular antigen test (CrAg) was positive. Lumbar puncture revealed pleocytosis and hypoglycorrhachia, and both CSF culture and CSF mNGS confirmed Cryptococcus neoformans infection. Successfully treated with amphotericin B cholesterol complex and flucytosine, satisfying E1 confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 67-year-old female with chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma presenting with recurrent fever, headache, and nuchal rigidity. Lumbar puncture revealed opening pressure of 240 mmH2O. CSF smear confirmed the presence of Cryptococcus neoformans, CrAg was positive, and mNGS confirmed Cryptococcus neoformans (77.78% relative abundance) with concurrent Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Diagnosed with concurrent cryptococcal and bacterial meningitis, satisfying E1 confirmatory criteria -> POSITIVE.
